cases.user_input: How are ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes differentiated on CT scans?
cases.response: Ischemic strokes appear as **hypodense (dark) regions** on CT scans, reflecting infarcted tissue from blocked blood supply [S1][S2]. Hemorrhagic strokes appear as **hyperdense (bright) regions** on CT scans due to acute bleeding forming a hematoma [S1][S2][S4]. These characteristic patterns—hypodense infarctions versus hyperdense bleedings—are the key visual markers used to differentiate the two stroke types on CT [S1].
